subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up: GPU choices & token mix
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@atlaslabs.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 2 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up: GPU choices & token mix

Hi Maria — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a few open items so we can produce a concise dedicated-capacity recommendation for Atlas Labs.

Summary from our conversation
- Target workloads: real-time chat + batched summarization jobs. Expected steady-state inference with predictable peak windows.
- Preferred deployment modes: leaning to Dedicated (customer-isolated GPU pool) with a Private VPC for network controls; on-prem is not needed at this stage.
- Cost sensitivity: want to balance latency vs unit cost — asked about H100 vs A100 tradeoffs.

Open items we need from you to finalize a sizing worksheet (attached):
1) Confirm peak TPS (requests/sec) for chat during peak hour and typical burst multiplier (e.g., 3x short spikes).
2) Provide a 7-day sample of request+token-size distribution (CSV is fine).
3) Any hard latency SLOs (p95/p99) for short (< 50 tokens) requests and for long (> 500 tokens) runs.
4) Expected concurrency per user/session (if you have a rough number).

Next steps I propose:
- You drop the traffic sample into the template I attached and send back — I’ll run a quick sizing model and come back with 2 configs (latency-optimized and cost-optimized).
- If helpful, we can do a technical deep-dive with our infra lead (Karthik) to validate perf targets.

Attachment: capacity_estimate_template.xlsx (simple TPS/token mix tab + notes)

Thanks — I’ll aim to return a first-pass config within 48 hours after we get the sample.

Best,
Nikhil Sharma

Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up: GPU choices & token mix

Hi Nikhil — thanks for the notes. Attached is a short export from our production window (7 days) and an annotated sample row to explain fields. Quick answers inline:

- Peak TPS: we see sustained peak of ~600 req/s during our busiest hour; short spikes hit ~1.8k for a few minutes (so ~3x).
- Token mix: ~80% of requests are very short (10–50 tokens), 15% medium (50–500 tokens), ~5% long-running summarization jobs (500–1,200 tokens).
- Latency SLOs: for chat (short requests) p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 250ms. For summarization jobs we target throughput over latency but p95 <= 2.5s is preferred.
- Concurrency per session: typical concurrent contexts per user are low (1–2), but our front-end will multiplex hundreds of user sessions across workers.

We're budget-conscious and evaluating A100s for cost, but the team is nervous about missing p99 on chat — curious what a hybrid pool looks like. Also confirm that VPC + dedicated capacity gives us control over outbound network egress.

Attachment: production_traffic_sample.csv

Happy to hop on a quick follow-up with Karthik next week if you think that's useful.

Thanks,
Maria Gomez
Head of Product, Atlas Labs
maria.gomez@atlaslabs.com

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2026 10:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up: GPU choices & token mix

Maria — this is great, thanks for the quick turnaround. Based on the sample and the SLOs you listed, here are two preliminary configurations and rationale. These are high-level; Karthik can run targeted benchmarks against samples if you want numbers validated.

Option A — Latency-optimized (recommended if p99 for chat is critical)
- Pool: Mixed fleet with H100 instances for the low-latency tier + A100s for cost-effective throughput.
- Example: 4 x H100 (for p99-sensitive short requests) + 8 x A100 (baseline throughput for medium/long jobs).
- Concurrency/batching: small batch windows for H100 (batch size 4–8, max latency budget 100–150ms), larger batches on A100 for summarization.
- Benefits: H100s reduce p99 tail for short requests; smaller H100 pool keeps cost contained.

Option B — Cost-optimized (if latency budget can be relaxed)
- Pool: All-A100 fleet sized to baseline throughput + autoscale headroom for spikes (burst to hosted fallback or to a warmed spare pool).
- Example: 16 x A100 with autoscale policy + a 3x burst allowance routed to hosted tier for short spikes.
- Concurrency/batching: aggressive batching for medium/long jobs; dynamic batching for short requests to satisfy p95.

Hybrid notes and recommendations
- Hybrid (A) gives the best chance to meet your p99 without the full cost of an H100-only deployment.
- We recommend configuring automatic fallback routing from Dedicated -> Hosted API for extreme spikes (the hosted tier can absorb short-lived 3x bursts without provisioning equivalent dedicated headroom).
- VPC: Dedicated + Private VPC will give you customer-managed subnets and egress controls — we’ll include a VPC network checklist if you proceed.

Next asks for us to finalize numbers
1) Confirm whether you want strict p99 guarantees (I’ll size to meet p99 target vs p95).
2) Any budget ceiling for monthly committed spend (so we can produce a baseline and an alternate lower-cost config).
3) Confirm whether hosted-fallback is acceptable for brief spikes (we’ll model cost both with and without fallback).

I attached a short PDF with the initial sizing math and cost assumptions (initial_sizing_v1.pdf). If that looks reasonable, I’ll coordinate a perf run with Karthik and propose a finalized config and an estimated monthly commitment.

If you want to schedule the tech deep-dive, Karthik is available Thursday afternoon or Friday morning PT.

Best,

Karthik — forwarding Atlas Labs thread. Can you run these quick checks before the call with Maria if we schedule: 
- Target H100 perf for short requests: get estimated p95/p99 for 10–50 token prompts with batch sizes 1/4/8.
- A100 throughput test for medium/long jobs: tokens/sec for 500–1,200 token workloads at typical batch sizes.
- Cost model: relative monthly cost delta between the proposed 4x H100 + 8x A100 mix vs 16x A100 (assume steady 600 TPS baseline + 3x spike allowance routed partially to hosted fallback).

Notes: Customer prefers Thursday afternoon or Friday morning PT — if you’re available, I’ll book a 45m session and include Maria + Rachel + Vanessa (ops).

Thanks — Nikhil
